sources.text:
Man shot by ICE appears in immigration court with bullet still lodged in neck, lawyers say
NEW YORK (TNND) — Oscar Belgal, the New York man shot by federal immigration officers last week, appeared remotely in immigration court Thursday.
His lawyers say he still needs surgery to remove a bullet lodged in the back of his neck. Federal officials previously described his injury as “superficial,” saying he was hit by a bullet or fragment.
Belgal, 28, a native of the Dominican Republic, barely spoke during the brief hearing, according to the Associated Press. His injury wasn’t visible on the video feed as he appeared from the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn, where his lawyers say he is being held in solitary confinement.
Karene Brown of the Legal Aid Society told Judge Dara Reid that Belgal has been on 24-hour lockdown without access to a phone to speak with his family. Brown said she had asked ICE to move him out of solitary confinement, but the agency had not honored the request. Reid said she had no say in where he is housed within the facility.
In a court filing obtained by ABC News, Belgal’s lawyers also said he has received only ibuprofen for pain. They said the left side of his face remains numb and that he has difficulty hearing in his left ear.
Belgal tried to speak to the judge about his living conditions, but his lawyer advised him not to and cut him off, the Associated Press reported.
Belgal was shot on Oct. 8 while in his car with his 5-year-old son. His lawyers allege that masked officers in civilian clothes approached the vehicle without identifying themselves, smashed a window and fired as Belgal tried to drive away.
The Department of Homeland Security said the officers believed their lives were in danger and fired after Belgal hit two government vehicles and accelerated toward them. NYPD body-camera footage shows officers arriving moments after the shooting.
Belgal’s lawyers filed a federal petition seeking his release. On Wednesday, a federal judge ordered the administration to explain why he should remain in custody and temporarily barred his deportation. His next immigration court hearing is scheduled for Oct. 29.
